findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread the escalation decision through orchestrator.route_criteria's bug_tier gate (the single seam both the assemble step and the batch-runner fan-in call), not only the assemble/precheck workflow op, so an escalated bug runs the full criteria set on every caller.
evidence: orchestrator.route_criteria lines 214-221: `bug_tier = ctx.ticket_type == 'bug'` then `if bug_tier and cid not in registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA: continue` — the actual restriction seam

findings.finding: The plan locates the escalation in 'the workflow_ops.py bug branch + the assemble step's criteria routing', but the load-bearing bug-tier restriction is not in the assemble step — it is in orchestrator.route_criteria, which keys unconditionally on ticket_type=='bug' and is 'the single routing seam' reached by BOTH the assemble step AND the batch-runner's project-criteria fan-in (docs/plan-review-gate.md:1100-1102). If the escalation flag is threaded only through the precheck/assemble ops and not into route_criteria's bug_tier gate, the batch-runner fan-in path would still restrict an escalated bug to BUG_TIER_CRITERIA, so the escalation would be incomplete (project/full criteria stripped).
findings.location: Approach → B1 / Scope ('criteria routing for the escalated path')
scenarios: An escalated bug whose project has an activated blocking project.* criterion: the assemble op reports full criteria, but the batch runner's independent route_criteria call still strips them under bug_tier — the escalated review silently runs the light set

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether B2's Gerrit bug-size criterion reuses the existing exec:"DET" routing + fail_mode + code_review/detectors.apply_failclosed verdict-assembly path (or justify a parallel mechanism, given the predicate keys on ticket type + diff size + attestation verdict rather than an engine_b changed-file detector).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:109 apply_failclosed — 'a MATCH → force verdict BLOCK per blocking_enabled … an ABSTAIN → block per blocking_enabled only when fail_mode == "closed" … a fail_mode:"open" criterion records the abstain in coverage but does NOT block'
docs/adr/0016-project-det-invariants.md:35-49 — data-driven detector→criterion routing + per-criterion fail_mode; 'project invariants default to fail-OPEN; the security class stays fail-CLOSED'
src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:214 criterion_for_detector; detectors.run_detectors buckets abstained/matches per criterion (detectors.py:52-99)

Plan B2 enumerates INFRA-FAIL-OPEN 'never BLOCK on infrastructure' vs FLAG 'must not fail open' but names no existing mechanism — absence of any reference to exec:"DET"/fail_mode/apply_failclosed in the plan text
findings.finding: B2's 'review-bot DET criterion' with its bespoke ACCEPTED/FLAG/INFRA-FAIL-OPEN verdict predicate does not reference the code-review gate's EXISTING data-driven DET-criterion framework, which already generalizes exactly this fail-open-vs-block distinction. code_review/registry.det_criteria() + criterion_for_detector() route exec:"DET" entries carrying a per-criterion fail_mode ('open'|'closed', ADR 0016), and code_review/detectors.apply_failclosed() is the consumer-side verdict mutator that BLOCKs a MATCH per blocking_enabled while an ABSTAIN only blocks when fail_mode=='closed' (else recorded as coverage, never blocks) — the same open/closed axis B2 re-invents as INFRA-FAIL-OPEN (never block) vs FLAG (block). The plan should confirm whether B2's criterion rides this existing routing/fail_mode/apply_failclosed path (adding a DET routing entry + a predicate) or deliberately builds a parallel mechanism, and justify a parallel build if chosen (B2's predicate keys on ticket type + diff line count + attestation verdict rather than an engine_b detector over changed files, so a full run_detectors fit is not obvious).
findings.location: Approach §B2 ('DET code-review criterion at Gerrit'; review-bot DET criterion) + Scope bullet 'review-bot DET criterion (vote pipeline)'
scenarios: Implementer writes a standalone bug-size vote check + its own fail-open/block branching, duplicating apply_failclosed's fail_mode semantics and diverging from the code-review gate's established DET verdict-assembly posture.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to B2 committing to one of: (a) express the bug-size check as a code_review DET criterion (routing entry with fail_mode, verdict adjustment via apply_failclosed), reusing the established MATCH=block / fail_mode-open=advisory semantics; or (b) explicitly note it is a distinct non-detector predicate that cannot ride run_detectors, and reuse apply_failclosed's fail-open/block posture rather than re-implementing verdict mutation.

findings.finding: B1's two escalation signals are asymmetric: --size-lines uses a >150 size threshold, but the no-flag signal escalates on mere PRESENCE of any non-test file_impact path — a proxy for 'touches source', not for 'oversized/complex'. The plan justifies file_impact as a deterministic no-diff signal but states no positive rationale for why presence-of-a-path approximates the substantive/complex fix the escalation targets.
